roleNote: An example of what you can build from kit components. Start from it, change it, or ignore it; layout is your choice. Follow `must` (kit look and accessibility); `defaults` are this example's suggestions, change any of them.
copyNote: Not exported from agentic-ds-kit. add copies the source into your app (components/patterns/agent-permissions/) with this contract beside it. You own the copy: replace the demo data, rearrange or drop sections, and keep the `must` lines.
intent: What each agent may do on its own, as a page: AppHeader, a PageHeader with a count of waiting requests and Ask, the pending kit PermissionRequest first (Grant / Deny, then one line), a Table of actions with each level as an icon plus a word and a ghost Edit, a Card with a Switch that makes every action ask first, and an AutonomyDial for the default level of new actions. Edit opens a kit Drawer with a card RadioGroup and, for an amount, a CurrencyInput under the group. Below 640 the nav opens in a Drawer from a Menu button, the Table becomes a drill ListView, Edit opens from the bottom and the dial is left out.

topBar.note: Default true: the page draws its own AppHeader, and below 640 a Menu IconButton opens the nav in a kit Drawer. Set false inside an app shell (e.g. AppShellPattern) that gives the header and nav; the page then renders only its main.

must: Use kit components from agentic-ds-kit for anything the kit has; no local cousins (request cards, level pickers, autonomy sliders, edit panels)
Semantic tokens only (agentic-ds-kit/tokens.css); no raw hex, no primitive --color-* ramps
At most one appearance="solid" mode="primary" Button per view: Grant on the page, Save level in the Edit Drawer
Do not restyle kit components; change them through their props, slots, and tokens

Render the page content inside a main landmark; the top bar is AppHeader (a header landmark), and below 640 the nav is reachable from a Menu button in a kit Drawer. With topBar={false} the surrounding app shell gives the header and nav
A waiting request is the kit PermissionRequest, first on the page, with its own Grant / Deny wording and one-line result
A level is always an icon and a word, never the icon or colour alone; a level set by workspace policy has no Edit and no drill
The amount for "Up to an amount" is a kit CurrencyInput under the RadioGroup, not inside an option
defaults: Demo is Northwind's billing agents: Collections agent asks to refund up to $500 without asking (now $250, until 22 Dec), and 4 actions across 2 agents
The request maps onto one scope (Refunds, write, $500 per refund, 30 days until 22 Dec), names the agent in requestedAt, and the one-line result shows the time
Granting raises the refunds row to Up to $500; while it waits the row shows "$500 requested"
The switch card sits beside the dial, top-aligned and as tall as its content
Below 640 Last used drops, the list shows the level word as the row value, and the Default for new actions dial is left out
